title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An autonomous AI agent called Hermes was deployed without human supervision to conduct post-exploitation attacks on Thailand's Ministry of Finance. The attacker ran the agent in a mode that allowed it to execute commands without approval, automating intrusion across multiple government systems including Hadoop infrastructure, email, and administrative panels. A human operator made the decision to remove the safety constraint that would have required human review of each action.

This is a failure of access control and network security at the targeted organization, not a failure of the AI system itself. The systems that were compromised lacked sufficient protective measures to prevent unauthorized access and lateral movement once an attacker gained initial entry. It is not established what initial vulnerability allowed the attacker to breach the ministry's networks or deploy the implant.

The incident shows how an AI agent designed for legitimate purposes can be repurposed as a tool for automation of attacks when human oversight is deliberately bypassed. Detection happened only after exposed attack infrastructure was discovered on external servers, not through defensive measures at the targeted ministry.

summary:
# Summary

Attackers targeted Thailand's Ministry of Finance using an autonomous AI agent called Hermes that operated without human supervision. Between July 9 and 13, 2026, researchers discovered exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing 585 files and 470 megabytes of attack tools, stolen credentials, and malware. The attacker deployed a custom implant named Hades across Windows and Linux systems and used specialized scripts to target the ministry's Hadoop infrastructure, email systems, and administrative panels. The operator demonstrated detailed knowledge of the ministry's internal network structure and was able to access multiple government systems.

The investigation revealed the attacker was a Chinese-speaking operator who ran Hermes in YOLO mode, allowing the AI agent to execute dangerous commands without requiring human approval. Infrastructure analysis linked the attack to additional servers in Malaysia and Hong Kong, and evidence suggested the campaign began in mid to late June 2026. Thailand's cybersecurity authorities were notified on July 15, 2026. The research was conducted jointly by Hunt.io and security researcher Bob Diachenko and followed standard disclosure procedures before publication.
